prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals (ideological framing removed)

Foundations, fiscal and tax
- Fiscal rules: balance the current budget and have debt falling as a share of GDP by year five; OBR oversight for fiscal events.
- No rises to National Insurance, Income Tax rates (basic/higher/additional) or VAT.
- Close tax loopholes: abolish non‑dom status, end offshore inheritance tax avoidance, close carried‑interest treatment, modernise HMRC to reduce avoidance.

Economy, business, innovation and infrastructure
- Industrial strategy with a statutory Industrial Strategy Council; sector plans (e.g., automotive, life sciences, creative, financial services).
- National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to crowd in private capital (3:1) for ports, gigafactories, steel, carbon capture and green hydrogen.
- Business tax roadmap; cap corporation tax at 25% for the Parliament; permanent full expensing; replace business rates in England.
- Ten‑year infrastructure strategy; National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority; accelerate planning for nationally significant projects; full gigabit and national 5G by 2030.
- Regulatory Innovation Office; National Data Library; binding regulation for frontier AI; ban sexually explicit deepfakes.
- Small business: tackle late payments, reform British Business Bank/regulation/procurement; support Post Office and Horizon redress.

Energy, climate, nature and water
- Zero‑carbon electricity by 2030: double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; invest in CCS, hydrogen, marine; Energy Independence Act.
- Nuclear: extend existing plants; deliver Hinkley Point C; progress Sizewell C and SMRs; maintain a strategic gas reserve.
- No new North Sea exploration licences; no new coal; ban fracking; close windfall tax loopholes and extend levy.
- Great British Energy (£8.3bn) to co‑invest and scale local power; upgrade grid; tougher retail market regulation and lower standing charges.
- Warm Homes Plan: £6.6bn to upgrade 5m homes; PRS minimum energy efficiency by 2030.
- Carbon border adjustment mechanism; mandatory credible transition plans for UK‑regulated finance and FTSE 100.
- Nature: new National River Walks, three National Forests, habitat expansion, circular economy.
- Water: special measures for polluting companies, bonus blocks, criminal sanctions, automatic fines, independent outlet monitoring.
- Farming: 50% of public sector food local or higher standard; reform ELM schemes; science‑led bovine TB plan; end badger cull.

Housing and renters
- 1.5m homes over the Parliament; restore mandatory housing targets; fund planners via higher non‑resident stamp duty surcharge.
- Brownfield first; strategic “grey‑belt” release with “golden rules”; new towns; cross‑boundary planning; reform CPO compensation.
- Permanent mortgage guarantee scheme for first‑time buyers; first‑dibs for locals.
- Private rented sector: abolish Section 21; empower challenges to unfair rent hikes; extend Awaab’s Law; building safety remediation focus.
- Leasehold reform: enact Law Commission package; ban new leasehold flats; make commonhold default; tackle ground rents and “fleecehold.”

Work, skills, immigration
- New Deal for Working People: ban exploitative zero‑hours, end fire‑and‑rehire, day‑one rights to sick pay/parental leave/unfair dismissal protection; Single Enforcement Body.
- Minimum wage to reflect living costs; remove lower adult age bands.
- Skills: Skills England; devolve adult skills; Technical Excellence Colleges; reform Apprenticeship Levy to a flexible Growth and Skills Levy; youth guarantee (training/apprenticeship/job support for 18–21s).
- Immigration: reduce net migration via reformed points‑based system; Border Security Command; more caseworkers; end hotel use; 1,000‑staff returns unit; negotiate additional returns agreements; end Rwanda scheme.

Health and care
- 40,000 extra NHS appointments per week (evenings/weekends); pool waiting lists; use independent sector capacity; workforce plan.
- Double CT/MRI scanners; deliver New Hospitals Programme; NHS innovation/adoption strategy; expand clinical trials via NHS app.
- Primary care: more GPs; face‑to‑face guarantee; modern booking; continuity incentives; pharmacist prescribing; wider direct/self‑referrals; trial Neighbourhood Health Centres.
- Dentistry rescue: 700,000 urgent appointments; contract reform; supervised tooth‑brushing (ages 3–5).
- National Care Service with national standards; “home first”; Fair Pay Agreement in adult social care; right to family visits.
- Mental health: 8,500 extra staff; Young Futures hubs in every community; modernise Mental Health Act.
- Public health: smokefree generation; youth vaping curbs; junk‑food ads restrictions to children; energy‑drink sales ban to under‑16s; online safety enhancements; gambling regulation reform.
- Reduce health inequalities; women’s health priority; new HIV action plan to end new cases by 2030.
- State pension triple lock retained; pensions reform to improve outcomes/productive investment.

Education and children
- 6,500 teachers in shortage subjects; CPD entitlement; reinstate support staff negotiating body.
- Curriculum/assessment review; stronger early numeracy and language; leadership programme; regional improvement teams.
- Replace single Ofsted grade with report cards; inspect MATs; annual safeguarding/attendance reviews.
- 3,000 school‑based nurseries; free breakfast clubs in every primary; mental‑health professionals in every school; cap branded uniform items.
- Arts/sport access: creative/vocational subject to 16; National Music Education Network; ticket‑resale protections; independent football regulator.

Crime, policing and justice
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee (more officers/PCSOs/specials); collaboration and procurement standards fund savings.
- Antisocial behaviour: Respect Orders; tougher fly‑tipping/vandalism penalties; specific offence for assaults on shopworkers.
- Knife crime: mandatory Youth Offending Team referral; curfews/tagging/custody for serious cases; ban zombie/ninja machetes; regulate online sales; Young Futures hubs; new offence of child criminal exploitation.
- Violence against women and girls: specialist rape units in every force; specialist courts; domestic‑abuse experts in 999; legal advocates; stronger stalking and anti‑spiking measures.
- Police standards: stronger HMICFRS powers; mandatory vetting/misconduct rules; safeguards on child strip‑searches; expanded fraud strategy; direct‑entry detectives.
- Courts/prisons: more prosecutors (Associate Prosecutors); sentencing review; build prison places; reduce reoffending via education, jobs, housing; probation governance review.
- Historical injustices: Hillsborough Law; Windrush Commissioner; act on Grenfell, Infected Blood and Covid Inquiry findings.

Governance, devolution and standards
- Independent Ethics and Integrity Commission; empower Ministerial Interests Adviser; modernise Commons procedures; ban MPs’ paid consultancy/advisory roles.
- House of Lords: remove hereditary peers; retirement at 80; participation standards; consult on a more representative second chamber.
- Elections: improve voter registration; address voter ID inconsistencies; votes at 16; tighten donation rules.
- Reset intergovernmental relations; Council of the Nations and Regions; uphold Windsor Framework; repeal/replace NI Legacy Act.

Foreign, defence and trade
- NATO and nuclear deterrent commitments; Strategic Defence Review; path to 2.5% of GDP on defence; Armed Forces Commissioner; scrap visa fees for non‑UK veterans (4+ years).
- Defence industrial strategy; procurement reform; support for Ukraine (including frozen asset use); AUKUS; calibrated China approach; defend Overseas Territories.
- Make Brexit work: improve EU trade (veterinary deal, MRAs, touring artists), security pact; targeted FTAs/sectoral deals; WTO/CPTPP engagement; OECD global minimum tax.
- Clean Power Alliance internationally; development refocus within FCDO; restore 0.7% GNI on aid when fiscally possible.
